key_insight: In EHR question answering, the more reasoning hops a question requires, the more likely large language models are to fail.
clinical_relevance: For clinical AI deployment, simple accuracy scores can hide weak performance on complex questions, so models should be risk-stratified by reasoning depth before use.
method: Annotated 313 clinician-written EHR Q&A pairs with a pre-specified 4-level hop-count taxonomy.
Evaluated 301 questions with Claude Sonnet (zero-shot and extended thinking) and replicated results in GPT-4o and GPT-5.4.
Checked whether lower performance at higher hops was explained by EHR truncation or context loss.
evidence_signal: Across three models, accuracy declined monotonically as hop count increased, with odds of a correct answer falling per added hop in every system tested.
watch_item: Hop count predicts failure risk, but it does not by itself prove how the model reasons, and results may not generalize to other EHR settings or task types.
paper_title: Compositional Reasoning Depth Predicts Clinical AI Failure: Empirical Evidence Consistent with Transformer Compositionality Limits in Electronic Health Record Question Answering
